Definition: of Latin origin; (little; but remotely from a derivative of G3973, meaning the same); Paulus, the name of a Roman and of an apostle:--Paul, Paulus.
BiblicalUsage: Paulos is Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles, called Saul until the Lord renames his ministry on the road to Damascus. He opens his letters as Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, in Romans 1:1 and 1 Corinthians 1:1, and in Galatians 1:1 he says his apostleship is not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father. His life and letters fill the book of Acts and thirteen epistles.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul matters because God chose the persecutor and made him the preacher, and the grace that saved him is the grace he preached. That is why I hold that no one is beyond the reach of the gospel that reached Paul.
